name: parca-parameter-fitting
title: ParCa — parameter fitting (Karr 2012 FitConstants reproduction)
question: Can viva-Mgen reproduce Karr 2012's parameter calculator (FitConstants) — computing the per-gene expression, decay and synthesis parameters the whole-cell model runs on from the real observed knowledge-base data, rather than hand-tuned guesses — and are those fitted parameters metabolically feasible?
hypothesis: Starting from the experimentally observed gene expression (Weiner 2003, decoded from the knowledge base) and the real per-gene half-lives, an analytic fit under the FitConstants constraints (RNA mass, DnaA/FtsZ held, net supercoiling) yields a per-gene parameter panel that reproduces the paper's expression kinetics and whose implied metabolic demand the iPS189 network can supply.
objective: Run the mycoplasma_parca composite: compute the fitted per-gene panel from the decoded knowledge base, report the fit summary (gene count, mRNA/rRNA half-lives, median synthesis rate), the metabolic demand it implies, and the expression↔metabolism feasibility closure.
description: This is the UPSTREAM study the seven figure studies depend on — it produces the per-gene expression/decay/synthesis parameters they consume (viva_mgen.parca, wired into viva_mgen.expression_defaults). It is a native reproduction of Karr 2012 FitConstants: observed expression + per-gene half-lives are decoded directly from the knowledge-base MCOS .mat (no MATLAB/Octave); the initialization + analytic QP fit apply the real FitConstants linear constraints (RNA-mass balance, DnaA/FtsZ expression held, net-supercoiling zero using the real ported constants); and the expression↔metabolism loop is closed by verifying the iPS189 FBA network can supply the ribonucleotide and amino-acid precursor demand in the fitted composition. Fidelity: genuine — every input is real decoded KB data; the nonlinear metabolism resource coupling + heuristic refinement of the original fmincon are the reduced part.

simulation_set.name: baseline
simulation_set.condition: Canonical ParCa fit via sims/run.py (recorded in .pbg/runs.jsonl).

expected_behavior.name: full-gene-panel
expected_behavior.en: The fit covers the full M. genitalium gene set (~522 of 525 genes).
expected_behavior.rationale: Karr 2012 tracks all ~480 protein-coding genes plus tRNA/rRNA (525 in genes.csv); the panel is computed over the full decoded set.

expected_behavior.name: mrna-halflife-realistic
expected_behavior.en: Mean mRNA half-life is a few minutes, as in the knowledge base.
expected_behavior.rationale: Decoded per-gene mRNA half-lives average ~4.6 min (bacterial mRNA t½ ~2-5 min).

expected_behavior.name: stable-rna-long-lived
expected_behavior.en: Stable RNAs (rRNA) are long-lived — orders of magnitude above mRNA.
expected_behavior.rationale: Decoded rRNA half-life is 1200 min (20 h), vs ~2.5 min for mRNA.

expected_behavior.name: metabolic-demand-at-rich
expected_behavior.en: The ribonucleotide demand is AT-rich (A+U dominant), reflecting the genome.
expected_behavior.rationale: M. genitalium's ~32% GC genome yields A+U ≈ 0.62 of the ribonucleotide demand.

expected_behavior.name: expression-metabolism-closed
expected_behavior.en: The iPS189 network can supply the fitted precursor demand (loop closed).
expected_behavior.rationale: Closure — the fitted expression's ribonucleotide + amino-acid demand is supplyable by the iPS189 FBA network alongside feasible growth (feasible = 1.0).
